Ten things I learned shipping a mobile app alone

Kenji MoriFollow8 min read

A year ago I quit my job to build a habit tracker. It now has 40,000 users and pays my rent. Here is what I would tell myself on day one.

1. Ship the boring version first

My first build had sync, themes and widgets. None of it mattered until reminders worked reliably, and reminders took three rewrites.

2. App review is a schedule, not a gate

Plan every release around a two-day review. Rejections are usually about one sentence in the description, so keep it plain.

3. Support email is product research

Every complaint is a free usability test. I answer each one myself and tag it, and the tags decide what I build next. You can read my notes on tagging for details.
